seoTitle: Tailscode: Claude Code, opencode & Oh My Pi on your Lock Screen
metaDescription: Claude Code, opencode and Oh My Pi on your Lock Screen. Approve, read diffs, price every turn. iPhone, iPad, Mac, Linux. No relay, no sign-in, no tracking.
heroHeadline: Your coding agents, live on the Lock Screen
heroSubhead: Send a prompt to Claude Code, opencode or Oh My Pi, pocket the phone, and watch the turn finish. Approve, answer and read the diff over your own tailnet, from the iPhone, iPad, Mac or Linux.
highlights: Live Activity per conversation on the Lock Screen
Approve, answer and read the diff from the phone
Every turn priced, every month totalled
Free, open source, no relay, no sign-in

features.title: The Lock Screen is the status board
features.body: A Live Activity per conversation shows what the agent is doing, for how long and how many tools it has run. An approval alerts you; a finished turn lingers with its outcome. Tap to land in the exact chat.

features.title: Approve with the edit in view
features.body: Allow once, always or deny, right under the diff, while the agent waits. A question arrives as a card you answer with a tap. Queue the next message, edit it before it goes, or stop the turn on the server.

features.title: Every machine, one board
features.body: All your servers' conversations in one list: live turns first, grouped by project. Subagents open in place inside the turn that spawned them; a compaction is a seam you can read.

features.title: A repository is read, never operated
features.body: Branch, drift from upstream, staged, changed and the real patch of any file, read from the machine that owns it. Nothing offers to commit or push: a change made from a phone is a change nobody reviewed.

features.title: Prices in dollars
features.body: Every conversation priced, every month totalled across machines by model, project and tool. Always marked an estimate: a subscription bills a flat fee, so the figure is API-equivalent value, never a bill.

features.title: Limits before the wall
features.body: Each provider's tightest window and its reset clock on Home and in a widget: Claude plan limits, Grok quotas, Ollama Cloud, DeepSeek balance. The board holds still while you read it.

features.title: One pill for model and effort
features.body: Which model and how hard it thinks are one decision: tap a level or slide to it, pin a pair, swipe to cycle. Ultracode burns a rainbow along the composer's edge.

features.title: Three agents, one app
features.body: opencode directly, Claude Code through claude-bridge, Oh My Pi through omp-bridge: two open-source companion servers. Every model Oh My Pi can reach is one picker away.

features.title: Native, and written not pasted
features.body: Programmatic UIKit on iOS, GTK4 on Linux, AppKit on the Mac, all Swift 6. Answers play out at a reading pace with nothing re-wrapping under you, and code copies byte-exact.

howItWorks.body: On the machine where you code, run claude-bridge's one-line installer: it downloads a prebuilt program (no Swift or git), starts it as a service and ends with a QR code. Prefer opencode or Oh My Pi? opencode serve and omp-bridge work the same way. All three are open source.
Install Tailscale on your devices, free for personal use. They see each other directly; the app checks your phone's tailnet address and which agent answers the address you type.

Scan the QR code the installer printed, open its link, or let Tailscode discover your servers. Send a prompt from the phone, follow it on the Lock Screen, sit down at the desktop and the same session is already there.

pricing.footnote: One purchase covers iPhone and Mac on the same Apple Account. The Linux client and the Mac build you compile yourself are free, open-source and complete: the unlock is how the work gets funded, not a wall around it.

faq.a: Yes. The free app is the complete core: one server, full chat, approvals and questions, attachments, models, forking, Live Activities, the analytics and the git surface. Tailscode Pro is a one-time $14.99 unlock for unlimited servers, concurrent Live Activities on iPhone, the delegate board (beta) and a supporter badge. There is no subscription, and the Linux client and a Mac build you compile yourself are free and complete.

A computer you code on, running opencode, Claude Code through claude-bridge, or Oh My Pi through omp-bridge; Tailscale (free for personal use) on that machine and on your phone; and the app. Set-up is three steps the app verifies as you go. No server yet? Tap 'Try the demo' on the first screen to explore every screen with sample conversations, no tailnet needed.

Not by Tailscode. Prompts, answers, diffs and files travel between your devices and your machines over your own Tailscale network, and never reach us. There is no Tailscode server between them and nothing to sign in to. The App Store apps do keep a random Midgar ID, report your Pro or tip purchase to our ledger and send anonymous More Apps counts; none of it is used for tracking, and the Linux app and the direct Mac build collect nothing. The privacy policy lists every row, and the source is public. Your agent still talks to its own model provider the way it always did; that part is between you and them. One optional exception: if your claude-bridge holds an Apple push key, Lock Screen updates ride Apple's push service and carry the conversation's title, its phase and tool counts.

It is built around Tailscale: set-up checks your tailnet, and the bridges admit a device signed into the same Tailscale account without a password. A server reachable some other private way (a LAN, another VPN) works with the server's password, but then the privacy claim rests on that route rather than on ours.

faq.q: Which coding agents does it support?
faq.a: opencode natively, 1.x or 2, with any provider you've configured in it; Claude Code through claude-bridge; and Oh My Pi through omp-bridge. The bridges are open-source Swift servers that expose a terminal agent as structured streaming sessions backed by your own subscriptions. Oh My Pi brings its whole provider catalog: Ollama Cloud, OpenCode Go, OpenRouter, Anthropic, xAI, DeepSeek and your local ollama.

faq.q: Is there a Mac and a Linux client?
faq.a: Yes: a native AppKit app for macOS 26, on the Mac App Store under the same purchase as the iPhone app, and a native GTK4/libadwaita app for Linux. Arch users install it from the AUR (`paru -S tailscode`); everyone else grabs the release tarball from GitHub. Both desktops add tiling splits and a global quick-ask hotkey; the Linux client and a Mac build you compile yourself also carry an embedded terminal and web and video panes, which the sandboxed Mac App Store build leaves out.

faq.q: How does the Lock Screen update when the app is closed?
faq.a: Two optional ways. claude-bridge can push Live Activity updates over Apple's push service. And when a turn ends while the app is closed, iOS holds a background request that the server answers only when the turn ends or stops for you (claude-bridge 1.13+, omp-bridge 0.7+, opencode 2), then posts the notification; that wait runs straight over your tailnet, not through Midgar or Apple. Background App Refresh off, or a force-quit, silences it, and Settings says so.

Tailscode Pro is a one-time $14.99 unlock for unlimited servers, concurrent Live Activities on iPhone, a supporter badge and the delegate board, a beta that hands routine tasks to a cheaper model and lets a verifier decide. The free app is the complete core forever, with one server.

faq.q: Where do pictures and clips get made?
faq.a: On a machine of yours running ComfyUI, reached over your tailnet: Qwen-Image or FLUX 3 Klein for pictures, LTX for clips. Tailscode is the brief, the stage and the shelf; the files stay in the machine's own output folder, and nothing leaves your tailnet.

faq.q: Can I watch the app my agent is building?
faq.a: Yes, with a Mac. A Mac running previewd, a small host that runs next to Xcode, builds the app on a simulator of its own and streams the screen; Tailscode draws it beside the conversation, keeps the last good picture under the compiler’s first error when a build fails, and hands that error to the agent in one tap. On Linux the pointer operates the app, and the Compare, Inspect, Quality, Matrix and Rewind lenses are built; the iPhone and the Mac show the picture.

All of it, under GPL-3.0: the iPhone app, both desktop clients, the engine (CodingAgentKit, a Swift 6 package that also runs on Linux), and both bridges (claude-bridge, omp-bridge). Build it yourself or grab it from the App Store.
